authorization: User requested a LangGraph implementation using OpenAI gpt-6.1-sol, authorized a supplied credential test without storing the key in the project, and requested a loopback after failed verification. This supplement defines the first executable orchestration component and isolated synthetic provider test, not public feature enablement.

delivery.core: Implement retrieval/allow_ai as a documented reusable Python LangGraph workflow using installed pinned LangGraph1.2.19, with exact immutable request binding, closed source-edit/explanation response schema, explicit consent boundary, bounded verification-repair edge, authoritative callback checks and content-free durable dispatch accounting.
delivery.integration: The graph is a callable component for a future Spring-authorized adapter, not a replacement authentication service. No new public HTTP endpoint, UI auto-apply/save, production document/corpus access, database migration or deployment in this component. Production mode stays OFF. Existing embedding/retrieval representation and SQL routing are untouched.
delivery.demo: Supply a runnable isolated CLI using only a repository-authored anonymous static Alloy fixture and the actual sandboxed DocumentWorkerMain parser/type/projection verifier. Initial SOURCE_EDIT and EXPLANATION support are explicit; typed slot operation DTOs, live document context, RAG grants and browser receipt application remain later integration gates. Do not call the whole A1/A3 product phase complete.

provider.identity: Only https://api.openai.com/v1/responses and exact request model gpt-6.1-sol. No alternate host/model, fallback, tool calls, remote embeddings, function execution, previous_response_id, provider conversation storage or SDK retry. Set store:false, stream:false, service_tier:default, reasoning.effort:low and bounded max_output_tokens. Account access is established only by the actual test outcome, not public model documentation.
provider.credential: Secret supplied through an ephemeral inherited FD or non-echo getpass directly into provider memory; never command arguments, environment variables, project files, .env, graph state, checkpoints, examples, journals, logs, trace payloads or subprocess inputs. Disable core dumps for the test process. No raw request/response/exception logging. Discard provider error bodies; report only fixed sanitized outcome codes and HTTP status. Ensure validator child receives no credential FD/environment.
provider.transport: TLS verification enabled; redirects and ambient environment proxies disabled. Enforce bounded serialized request/response and connect/read/overall deadline. One provider call active per exclusively owned ledger. No automatic retry on HTTP/auth/rate-limit/network/read/timeout/refusal/incomplete response or uncertain dispatch.
provider.budget: For this isolated standard-tier test, cap total worst-case reserved spend at100000 micro-USD, each of at most two calls at50000 micro-USD. Pinned conservative bound assumes <=8192 billed input/cache-write tokens at2.50USD/M, <=2048 total output including reasoning tokens at10USD/M and up to10percent regional premium:45056micro-USD <=50000. Enforce a conservative serialized ASCII request ceiling4096bytes plus4096 token overhead reserve, outputcap2048, no tools or premium service tier. Unknown tariff/version/account surcharge or larger payload denies paid admission. Keep the tariff assumptions explicit; real provider billing is not proved. Outputusage/tier is inspected without storing content; missing/uncertain usage retains full reservation. No observed usage refund is needed in this first conservative ledger.
provider.response: Require a completed response containing exactly one supported text answer, no refusal/tool/action items; permit ignored reasoning metadata only without executing or logging it. Require exact requested model or documented snapshot identity for gpt-6.1-sol; no family substitution. Decode strict duplicate-free JSON with bounded depth/bytes and closed keys: kind SOURCE_EDIT or EXPLANATION, source string, explanation string. SOURCE_EDIT must contain nonempty bounded source; EXPLANATION must have empty source and is always AI_SUGGESTION. Model output cannot assign validation status or trusted evidence.

graph.topology: prepare -> consent -> dispatch -> verify -> (review_ready | repair_prepare -> consent -> dispatch -> verify | terminal). Use actual StateGraph conditional edges, not a recursive unbounded agent. Graph recursion limit is a backstop; authoritative attempt count and consumed dispatch identities enforce at most two external calls. No graph RetryPolicy, cache, store, persisted messages or checkpointer; thread/callback configuration supplied by callers is rejected if it enables external tracing or arbitrary callbacks.
graph.state: Graph state contains only bounded input/proposal/diagnostic values, opaque trusted binding digest, prepared exact payload digest, attempt count and status. The provider/key, verifier, budget journal, clock and authorization/consent capabilities stay outside serialized graph state. Caller cannot resume at arbitrary nodes or forge accepted validation flags through the supported Runner interface.
graph.authority: Trusted host callbacks recheck current binding/session/rights/deadline before consent, before dispatch, after response, after verification and before final publication. A stale or denied result is terminal and cannot be repaired. The synthetic harness identifies itself as a private development fixture; it is not evidence of real Spring authorization. A future production adapter must resolve immutable owner/context through existing Spring boundaries.
graph.consent: The normal runner requests exact prepared payload plus hash/attempt/model for explicit consent on every dispatch, including the repair payload. Declining consent makes no provider call. The user-authorized one-off synthetic test may use an explicit harness grant restricted to the fixed authored fixture, original intent and closed sanitized diagnostic codes, with at most one repair; it is not a reusable consent bypass for arbitrary documents. No failed response text, private diagnostic contents or retrieved data is appended automatically.
graph.loopback: Only deterministic closed-schema/parse/type/projection verification failures may take the repair edge, and only after one completed provider call. The repair prompt contains the original authorized fixture/context plus closed sanitized failure codes and asks for corrected output. Recompute exact payload digest, renew consent/recheck authority and reserve the second attempt. Verify the replacement from scratch. A second invalid result terminates INVALID_PROPOSAL. No partial invalid artifact reaches review-ready.
graph.terminal_failures: Authentication/permission/session expiry, budget or ledger error, build identity mismatch, validator unavailable/timeout, provider refusal/incomplete result, rate limit, network/unknown dispatch and malformed provider envelope are terminal. They never become successful verification or automatic repair. Cancellation prevents later publication but does not assert remote cancellation/billing cessation.
graph.publication: Only deterministic SOURCE validation success yields a review-ready source proposal, with exact candidate hash and worker result evidence. Preserve BLOCK_SUPPORTED versus TEXT_ONLY projection. EXPLANATION yields a suggestion with no parser/type/equivalence claim. Neither result changes accepted history or grants automatic application/save. Graph returning normally alone is not success; callers inspect the closed terminal status.

journal.location: Operator-supplied private absolute ledger path outside the project, with regular owner-only files, no symlink ancestors, dedicated short directory and one exclusive lock covering the runner/network work. The example/test may use a fresh owned /tmp directory. No database access or SQL is introduced by this isolated harness; a production accounting store remains a future parser-routed integration.
journal.contents: Only schema, operation/attempt IDs, reservation amount, consumed dispatch state and sanitized status. No prompt, source, key, header, response, explanation, provider token or raw exception. Use atomic fsynced writes plus directory fsync. Persist budget reservation AND consumed dispatch intent before opening the network connection. A crash after intent remains spent/unknown on restart; no refund, resend or reset.
journal.replay: One externally issued operation ID is permanently consumed for this ledger once its first dispatch is recorded. Reusing it cannot send again, including after timeout/restart or changed payload. Attempts have unique derived identities and the two-call bound is enforced outside graph data. New operation IDs still consume the same installation ledger ceiling. Existing malformed/oversized/ambiguous/untrusted journal fails closed, never repaired by deletion or empty initialization. Other identities/new journals are outside this isolated operator trust boundary, not a public quota-control claim.

verification.worker: Invoke existing compiled dev.allow.worker.DocumentWorkerMain through fixed bubblewrap/prlimit sandbox with network unshared, no arbitrary argv/path or source execution outside it. Strict newline JSON frame with matching protocol/request nonce, operation VALIDATE, exact candidate {mode:SOURCE,source:...}, fixture empty baseArtifact/ownedIdInventory and fixed policy. Empty fixture ownership is never used for production documents.
verification.limits: Source <=32768UTF8bytes; existing stricter artifact/node/depth/type/projection limits preserved. Worker stdout <=1MiB and stderr discarded or bounded without source disclosure. Hard worker timeout<=10seconds or remaining whole-job deadline, fixed CPU/memory/process limits, kill/reap owned process group before release. No stdout capture unbounded in memory. Hash relevant compiled classes/dependencies/solver/helper before and after; mismatch is unavailable, not invalid.
verification.diagnostics: Only allowlisted diagnostic categories (SCHEMA_INVALID, SOURCE_PARSE_INVALID, SOURCE_TYPE_INVALID, SOURCE_PROFILE_INVALID) feed loopback. Detailed parser/source/path strings stay local or are omitted; invalid schema output is not pasted into repair prompts. A real valid/invalid/valid fixture verifies the repair path through actual Java parser/type/projection checks.

formal_first.required: Six exact-hash council decisions (2Terra,2Sol,2Astra), then two clean pinned Lean4.34.1 builds before any production Python/Java/JS/TS changes. Original37-policy model remains unchanged; supplement models bounded loopback, fresh consent, terminal nonrepair failures, pre-dispatch consumed identity and conservative reservation.
formal_first.limits: Finite policy only; authentic callbacks/clock, OS/filesystem fsync/locking, provider protocol/pricing, cryptography, sandbox and deterministic verifier remain trusted. No implementation refinement, distributed exactly-once billing, privacy guarantee or commercial promotion.

acceptance: Actual compiled LangGraph invokes valid fixture -> one call -> verification -> REVIEW_READY; invalid then valid -> exactly two calls and renewed exact consent; repeated invalid -> INVALID_PROPOSAL after two; no infinite loop.
Schema-invalid outputs take bounded repair; unavailable worker/provider, malformed envelope, auth, stale binding, expired job, denied consent, budget/ledger failure and uncertain dispatch never loop.

Ledger crash/reopen, concurrent ownership and same operation replay cannot resend; reservations survive unknown failure and new operation cannot exceed aggregate bound; malformed/linked/insecure journal denies network.

Mock HTTP transport verifies exact OpenAI endpoint/model/store:false/no tools/no redirects/proxies/retries, output/frame bounds, sanitized errors and credential absent from graph state/journal/repr/output/child environment. No real key is written to any test fixture.
Actual sandboxed source valid/invalid/repair integration with matching build/protocol hashes, bounded termination and no accepted-document/database mutations.
